r0.why: Ancient algorithm, prime definition, marking multiples from 2, unmarked are primes in 1,2,5,9

r1.why: Step-by-step list, mark 2p,3p.., next unmarked p, stop, why p is prime all in 10-16

r2.why: Constant-step multiples, only additions, key distinction from trial division, 15 marked twice, primes for free in 3,4,17,18,43

r3.why: Start at p squared, stop when p squared > n, odd-only with 2p steps, in original algorithm: 19-22

r4.why: Nicomachus 2nd c CE, Eratosthenes 3rd c BCE, efficient for small primes, arithmetic progressions, benchmark in 6,7,8,45

r5.why: O(n log log n), memory and cache issues, segmented sieve steps, O(sqrt n) space with same time in 28-37

r6.why: Trial division confusion, generates composites directly, worse complexity, Turner 1975 sub-optimal in 40-44
